summary: Save writes a temp file and renames it over the target, but it drops the os.Rename error and returns nil. When the rename fails, the caller is told the settings were saved when they were not, and the .tmp file is left behind. This contradicts the story and criterion 2. No test covers the failing-rename path.

findings.title: Rename error is discarded, so Save reports success when nothing was saved
findings.detail: If os.Rename fails (for example, path is a directory, or the target is on another filesystem or read-only), Save still returns nil. The old file is unchanged but the caller believes the new settings were persisted, and path+".tmp" is left on disk. The story requires Save to return an error when the settings were not saved, and criterion 2 expects an error.
findings.fix: if err := os.Rename(tmp, path); err != nil { _ = os.Remove(tmp); return err }; return nil

findings.title: No test for the failing-rename case in criterion 2
findings.detail: Only the happy path is tested. No test makes the rename fail (for example, by making path an existing directory) or checks that Save returns an error and the old content is unchanged, so the dropped error went unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a test that creates a directory at path (or an existing file whose directory is read-only), calls Save, asserts a non-nil error, and asserts the original content and no leftover .tmp file.

criteria.evidence: TestSaveLoad saves Settings{EUR, 20} to a temp path and Load returns an equal value; evidence/criterion-1.jsonl.
save.go:18 discards the os.Rename error and save.go:19 returns nil, so a failing rename returns no error. No test covers this case.
